reference.title: WH-guide-BACnet
reference.shortdesc: These elements are reused only within the BACnet Guide.

section.title: Notes and paragraphs
section.p: A BACnet client can send a request to a BACnet controller to dynamically create this component by using either an Object Id or Object Type. Optionally, the request may simultaneously specify initial values for one or more of a specified set of component properties.
section.note: This single extension applies to both COV and Interval data collection and may be used in place of the deprecated COV and Interval Trend Log Extensions for this data type.
section.p:
Only the following read-only properties qualify for initial value setting during object creation. Requests that include non-qualified properties from the client cause a request to fail.
Device Status Facets
Discovery History Type

li.p: Disconnect All disconnects all connected hub-accepting connections on the Hub Function and direct-initiating and -accepting connections on the Node Switch.

entry.div: Provides a numeric index into the property array. Applies only to an arrayed property, such as Priority Array, otherwise it defaults -1 for no index.
Displays the Media Access Control (MAC) address.
Reports the frequency with which data are imported from a remote trend log (or trend log multiple) into a history (or histories). Data import occurs at intervals, daily or when requested.

li.p: DeviceID changes the device ID in the device.
Delete sends a delete-object request to the remote BACnet device, which removes the BACnet object from the remote BACnet device.
li.note: The Delete key on the keyboard performs a local delete only. The delete keyboard action removes the selected BACnet object from the AWS device Config folder but it does not send a delete-object request to the remote device.

li.p: Events retrieves the current event information and sends it to the alarm console.
ESumm opens the Get Enrollment Summary window. This window

property.proptype: Accept Uris Node Switch and Priority Array

propdesc.div: Identifies the possible URIs that an initiating SC node can use to make a direct connection to this node. The values in this property are sent in the address resolution ack message.

Indicates the current state of the trend log based on the Active Period.
true indicates the log is active.
false indicates the log is no longer active because the current time is outside the Active Period.
Defines the Supervisor PC’s network adapter or VPN connection.
Serves as a collective property name for Network Number, MAC Address, and MAC address style.

Turns on and off the configuration of standard synchronization intervals for controller stations.
true sets up the same time synchronization interval in each host controller station.
false allows a different time synchronization interval for each host controller station.

property.proptype: Always Request By Reference Time reused 3 times

propdesc.div: Configures if the driver should always use the Reference Time to request records.

property.proptype: Application Software Version Device Object, Local Device (3x)

propdesc.div: Reports the version of the manufacturer’s software running on the device.

property.proptype: Backup Failure Timeout all three local devices

propdesc.div: Specifies the time the server device must wait before deciding that the client has given up, and can leave backup/restore mode. The client writes this to the server prior to beginning the backup/restore procedure.

property.proptype: Backup Preparation Time all three local devices

propdesc.div: Reports the time taken, after receiving a restore request, to gracefully shut down the station and close files before beginning the backup.

property.proptype: Backup and Restore State all three local devices

propdesc.div: Shows the current status of any backup or restore operation. The driver displays Idle when no operation is active. This changes to Preparing for backup and so forth.

property.proptype: Bacnet Comm reused in the 3 network topics

propdesc.div: Contains BACnet communication properties, which are documented in a separate topic.

property.proptype: Bacnet Status Flags, Status Flags, Status Flag used 30 times

propdesc.div: Configures four status flags for BACnet. These options are available to enable detection of specific status conditions.

property.propvalue: read-only or an array of check boxes

propdesc.div:
For writable types, provides an array of check boxes that configure the specific priority levels externally exposed to BACnet for the purpose of accepting writes. Included are all controls to clear or select.
This property is dimmed if the export Type is read-only, such as for Analog Input or Binary Value.
Each priority level (1-16) that you enable for BACnet writes results in that InN input on the source component to be linked to this Bacnet export descriptor component. These links appear as nubs when viewing the source writable point in its wire sheet view.
Do not select any priority level already linked or in use by the system, otherwise control contention occurs.
After you add a BACnet export descriptor you can configure additional properties accessible in its Property Sheet, along with those that are available in the Add and Edit windows.
Configures the size of a buffer.

property.proptype: Character Set BacnetAwsDevice, BacnetDevice, Local Device (3x)

propdesc.div: Defines the character set supported, with other selections: IBM/Microsoft DBCS, JIS C 6226, ISO 10646 (UCS-4), ISO 10646 (UCS-2), ISO 8859-1, and Unknown.

property.proptype: Conversion Proxy Extensions (4x), New point window (2x)

propdesc.div: Configures the facets to use when converting values from device facets to point facets.

property.proptype: Cov Increment, covIncrement Analog Input, Output Value, Trend Log descriptors
property.propvalue: number only for analog object types (Analog Input, Analog Output, Analog Value, Analog Value Priority, Loop, defaults to 1.00)

propdesc.div: Specifies the minimum COV required before a COVNotification is issued to subscriber BACnet COV-clients.

property.proptype: Cov Resubscription Interval Trend Log extensions

propdesc.div: Specifies the length of time that the extension waits before initiating a re-subscription request.

property.proptype: Cov Subscriptions Devices, New device window,

propdesc.div: Reports the number of active COV client subscriptions to the device.

property.proptype: Database Revision Device Object, Local Devices (total 4x)

propdesc.div: Reports the version of the database.

property.proptype: Data Type Proxy Extensions and New windows (total of 9x

propdesc.div: Reports the ASN (Abstract Syntax Notation) data type for a device property. The driver automatically converts values to this appropriate type. For example, an analog input present value is an ASN REAL that can be interpreted by a string point as a character string. ENUMERATED is another example.

property.proptype: Device Type, deviceType all the descriptors
property.propvalue: (optional) text only for some object types (Analog Input, Analog Output, Binary Input, Binary Output, Multi-state Input, Multi-state Output)

propdesc.div: Defines the type of physical input or output. This might apply mostly to exported Ndio points where each point corresponds to a physical device.

Uniquely identifies the object in the system.
When you upgrade a BACnet driver or drop in a BACnet network from the palette, the driver automatically sets this 128–bit universally unique identifier (UUID) to a random value.
You should not need to change this property. The driver uses it behind the scenes.

property.proptype: Enumeration List Devices (3x) and Local Devices (3x)

propdesc.div: Lists the BACnet properties that can be exported to configure data exchange. This Extensible Enum List provides access to each property's configuration facets.
Turns detection of an input event on (true) and off (false) for analog, binary and multi-state descriptors.

property.proptype: Event State (local device and trend logs) at least 18–19x

propdesc.div: Reports the status of the event.
Sets up a folder array.

property.propvalue: ord (defaults to the format used is the numeric handle instead of slot, which is better if the source object gets renamed)

propdesc.div: Defines the location of the source component or file using standard file Ord notation. In an Edit window, you can access a more meaningful ord by clicking the right-side folder control. This produces a popup Select Ord window, showing the component’s location in the station’s component tree hierarchy.

Provides the special manager views to associate devices and points (local objects) with BACnet objects (exported objects). You discover objects or add them using the New button.
The Bacnet Export Manager (plugin) topic documents this table.

property.proptype: Firmware Revision Device Object, Local Devices (4x)

propdesc.div: Reports the version of the device firmware.

property.proptype: History Id (BACnet)BacnetEventLogImport, Bacnet History Import, Bacnet Trend Log Multiple Import (2x)

propdesc.div: Displays a combination of the station name and history name.

property.proptype: History Name (Bacnet Trend Log Ext) used 17x

propdesc.div: Defines a pattern for deriving the name of the history created by this extension. It can be static text or a simple pattern that allows the actual history name to be derived from the context. The default value (%parent.name%) sets the history name in the Id to the name of the parent of this extension. Changes to this property cause the format to be reapplied and the history Id in the history config is to be updated.

property.proptype: History Policies Used by the three networks

propdesc.div: Configures the history network extension, which is documented in a separate topic.
Configures when to clean up connections.

Controls data collection behavior for this Trend Log component.
If the Interval value is set to 0, the driver collects trends when a change of value (COV) on the parent point occurs. The subscription lifetime is equal to twice (2x) the value of the COV Resubscription Interval property.
If the Interval value is set to any number greater than 0, the driver collects trend data at the specified time interval.

property.proptype: Interval Offset used in the three local devices

propdesc.div: Specifies an offset from the beginning of the interval at which to send the periodic time synchronization messages. If Align Interval is false, the driver ignores this property.
Reports the reason for the last restart.
Reports when a backup .dist file was last restored by a remote BACnet Workstation client. If never, all timestamp properties show asterisks (*).
Defines a maximum record number to process.

property.proptype: List Of Object Property References export/import descriptor and BACnet schedules (4x)

propdesc.div: Provides a standard Bacnet ListOf sequence, which contains a non-indexed sequence of references related to the schedule.

property.proptype: Local Device used in the three networks

propdesc.div: Contains device properties, which are documented in a separate topic.
Describes the device location.
Reports the name of the local history component.

property.propvalue: text, BFormat (Baja Format) syntax (defaults to %name%, which recreates the BACnet name of the trend log object) or a combination of text and BFormat.

propdesc.div:
Defines the format string script for returning a local history. This is the name of the history initially created and populated by the trend log data and includes, typically, the name of the BACnet device component and the BACnet trend log object.
For example: %parent.parent.displayName% %name% could define the name of a VAV fan: J7Bnet BldgA_VAV1_Fan.
You can modify the default BFormat with other BFormat scripting. You could enter static text for the history name—or, some combination of static text and valid BFormat scripting text.
In the case of trend log multiples (BacnetTrendLogMultipleImport), the default %name% value results in histories named using the BACnet name of the trend log multiple object, with underscore delimiters between the BACnet names of each _object_property record.

property.proptype: Local History Names 2 log import components and one other (3x)

propdesc.div: Reports the names of local trend logs.

property.proptype: Max Records Per Request BacnetEventLogImport, Bacnet History Import, Bacnet Trend Log Multiple Import (2x)

propdesc.div: Defines the maximum number of records that can be archived in this trend log. The Framework asks for 10 records per request.

property.proptype: Max Segments Accepted three local devices

propdesc.div: For a single segment, defines the number of characters the device supports.

property.proptype: Name (BACnet with object id and instance number) (6x)
property.propvalue: text in the format (for points, defaults to presentValuePoints)

propdesc.div:
Identifies the object (point, export folder, etc.) including an Object Id and Instance Number or property identifier, which ensures a unique name.
This name is in the format: objectType_<instance number> For example and Event State may be named: AHU1–Frz_Stat-eventState.
Refer also to Object Id, Instance Number.
Contains network-related properties. Refer to separate topics in this document.
Specifies the notification class used for routing when handling and generating event notifications for this object.

property.proptype: Number of Apdu Retries used in 3 local devices

propdesc.div:
Defines the maximum number APDU retransmissions.
Works for both client and server operations. For a small IP-based network, an optimal setting may be: 1 retry.

property.proptype: Number of States MSO, MSI, MSV(3x)

propdesc.div: Defines the number of states required by the Bacnet Multistate Input component.

property.propvalue: text in the format name.name.name.name (default includes the entire component path in the station using period (“/) delimiters between parent.child levels)

propdesc.div:
Identifies a BACnet object. This name should be unique within this specific device.
For components, this name includes the entire component path under the station’s Config using period (.) delimiters between parent.child levels. This enforces (externally) the BACnet requirement for unique names for all objects in a device.
For a proxy point, this is the default name in the station.
You can shorten or edit Object Name, however, each Object Name must be unique among all server descriptors under the Export Table.

property.proptype: Object Property Reference Bacnet Event Enrollment Descriptor, Trend Log

propdesc.div: Contains the properties related to the referenced object.
Reports the type of object.

property.proptype: Out of Service (Bacnet Analog Input Descriptor, as well as configuration analog input, analog output, analog value, binary input, binary output, binary value, loop, and more) 17x

propdesc.div:
Affects only the BACnet exposure and access to the source component. If the source (exported) component is a proxy point, the equivalent Enabled property in its ProxyExt is not affected.
true writes the point’s current value to the Present Value property. Often, a remote BACnet client sets (or clears) this Out of Service state.
You can set this property to false if needed.
Reports the type of port (Ethernet, MS/TP, etc.).
Defines the ORD (address) for the point.
Identifies the polarity related to an input. Values are: Normal and Reverse.
Represents a BACnet list containing a non-indexed sequence of objects of a particular BACnet data type.

property.proptype: Present Value (in a control point extension)3x

propdesc.div: While Out Of Service is set to true, this property reflects the last written Present Value.
Sets up an array of object identifiers that identify priority values.

Specifies a number in the Recipient List for the station. This integer from the BACnet Notification Class object of the sending device, must match this ID in the Alarms device extension of the receiving device.

property.proptype: Priority for Writing (export/import descriptors and BACnet schedules) 8x

propdesc.div: Reports schedule priority, which defaults to 16.

Identifies a particular element in an array of stored properties. For example the ObjectList is stored as an array of object identifiers.
This value applies only to an arrayed property, like Priority Array. For example, if the point proxies priority level 7 of a priority array input for a binary output point, this value is 7.
The Present Value property is not an array. For all properties that are not arrays, use an array index of -1.

Defines the specific data item being proxied. Often, this is Present Value or Event State. This unique numeric value correlates to and identifies the data item. For example, the number 85 correlates to a present-value property.Changing this ID on an existing BACnet proxy point can produce undesirable results, especially if the change assigns a different control point type. Instead, make a new proxy point.
Expands to identify all the available BACnet object types supported by this version of .
Displays the current BACnet protocol level.
Expands to identify all the available BACnet device services supported by this version of .
Displays the version number of the BACnet protocol.
Defines the timestamp the system uses to include records in the trend log.

Provides information when an error interrupts communication with a device.
No Fault Detected indicates that things are OK.
Unreliable Other indicates that the exported BACnet object appears in fault. This might happen, for example, if the source (exported) component is a proxy point under some other driver, and device communications are down or if the point has been disabled.
In this case, the BACnet export descriptor retains a status of ok.
Sets up a number to serve as the Present Value default.
Defines the alarm recipients to receive notification that the station restarted.
Reports the time taken, after receiving a restore request, to gracefully shut down the station and close files before beginning the dist file installation.
Reports the time taken, after completing a dist file install from a restore, for the station to restart and become responsive.
Indicates the type of message segmentation the device supports. If a message exceeds the Max Segment Accepted length, the device must be able to break it into segments or part of the message is lost.
Adjusts which property types in a target BACnet schedule object the system writes to upon an export from a weekly schedule component.
Indicates the condition of the BACnet schedule.
Identifies the local station ORD for the schedule.
Reports the current condition of the network.
Specifies the time of device restart based on the time of day (Time), a sequence number (SeqNum) or a date and time (DateTime).

property.proptype: Time Range, Start Time (BacnetDestination, Event Saver) 3x

propdesc.div: Configures when to start the function.

property.proptype: Time Range, End Time (BacnetDestination, Event Saver) 3x

propdesc.div: Configures when to end the function.
Configures how frequently the software sends the time synchronization messages.

Define the devices to receive time synchronization messages from the driver. This list of recipients is for periodic time synchronization messages. You add to and remove entries from this list using the right-click addElement and removeElement actions. Entries in this list are BacnetRecipients. They can be either a device object identifier, or a BACnet address.

Selects local time or universal time.
Local Time uses the current time at the Supervisor station location.
UTC Time uses Greenwich Mean Time. It does not observe daylight saving time.

property.proptype: Total Record Count (Bacnet Trend Log Ext) 16x

propdesc.div: Indicates the total number of records collected by the Trend Log object since creation. When the value of Total Record Count reaches its maximum possible value, the next value it takes is zero.
Specifies which status transitions are sent, where the default is all but toAlert.

Identifies the type of BACnet object, for example, Analog Input, Analog Output, Calendar, Schedule, Structured View, File, Trend Log, BooleanWritable or other.
Writable components typically offer more type selections than read-only points, such as:
Two read-only: input or value type, e.g. Binary Input or Binary Value object.
Two writable: output or prioritized value type, e.g. Binary Output or Binary Value Prioritized object.
The screen capture shows an example of type selections when exporting an NdioBooleanWritable point.
Reports the unit of measure for the entity.
Reports the frequency of updates.

property.propvalue: true or false If the device was discovered, and station database determined that the device indicates support for server-side COV, this property defaults to true. Otherwise, it defaults to false indicating that no proxy points under the device use COV.

propdesc.div:
Enables (true) and disables (false) a device’s support for COV (change of value) as a way to monitor proxy point values.
Assuming the device supports subscription to the COV service, true triggers the driver to attempt the necessary updates (proxy subscriptions) to the value of each point using the BACnet COV subscription to the device. If the subscription attempt succeeds, the Read Status property of the point’s BacnetProxyExt displays COV. If the subscription attempt fails, the driver uses normal polling and the Read Status property shows Polled.
When true, individual proxy points under the device may use COV subscriptions, depending on their assigned tuning policy.
When false, the driver ignores any proxy subscription updates.
Indicates if the system uses COV Property notification services (true) to receive data about points in this device for which COV Property is supported.

property.proptype: Use CRL Distribution Point in Issuer

propdesc.div: Uses the URL defined in the issuer certificate for retrieving CRLs.

Lists the recipients for periodic Time Synchronization messages. You can add and remove entries to this list using the right-click addElement and removeElement actions. Entries in this list are BacnetRecipients. They can be either a device object identifier, or a BACnet address.
Reports an identifier for the vendor’s device.
Reports the vendor number.

property.propvalue: hours minutes seconds (defaults to ten seconds)

propdesc.div: Defines how long a connection waits without success to establish a web socket connection before concluding that the attempt failed.
Defines how to write Enum data as Unsigned: ENUMERATED or as an INTEGER.

Indicates if the proxy extension is read-only or can be written to.
read only indicates the proxy extension cannot be written to.
writable or ok indicates that the proxy extension can be written to.
For writable proxy extensions, this property indicates either that the last write occurred within the effective tuning policy period or, if a write operation failed, it provides descriptive text.
For example, if you create a writable point for a read-only object (say, a NumericWritable for presentValue of an Analog_Input object) and attempt to write from the system, the write status may show: Property:Write Access Denied. If the error is actually a BACnet error, the colon-separated format contains the error class and error code returned by the device.
